launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.summary: Brooklyn's 526-acre flagship park combines Long Meadow, a 60-acre lake, wooded ravines, playgrounds, sports, a zoo, carousel, skating and splash play in one large landscape.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.hours: Open daily 6 AM-1 AM; individual attractions and facilities keep separate hours.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.parking: There is no dependable general visitor lot. Street parking around the perimeter is limited, so subway, bus, walking, or biking is usually easier. Choose the entrance nearest your destination before arriving.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.arrival: Grand Army Plaza works for the north end and Long Meadow; Bartel-Pritchard Square serves the southwest side; Ocean Avenue and Flatbush Avenue entrances are better for the zoo, Children's Corner, and Lakeside.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.restrooms: Seasonal and year-round comfort stations are spread across the park, including near the Picnic House, Boathouse, Children's Corner, Lincoln Road, and Lakeside. Confirm the nearest open facility on the official map.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.cost: Park entry is free. The zoo, carousel, skating, boat rentals, concessions, and some programs charge separately.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.accessibility: Major entrances and many paved routes are accessible, but the park is hilly and some woodland paths are uneven. Accessible facilities and entrances should be matched to the destination.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.dogs: Dogs must generally be leashed. Designated off-leash hours and areas include portions of Long Meadow, the Nethermead, and Peninsula Meadow; Dog Beach is for water access, not an all-day off-leash zone.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.family: Strong family choices include Children's Corner, multiple playgrounds, the carousel, zoo, Lakeside splash pad, lake, and broad lawns. Distances are large, so choose one or two zones per visit.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.transit: The 2/3 serves Grand Army Plaza; B/Q serves Prospect Park and nearby east-side entrances; F/G serves 15 St-Prospect Park. Several buses follow the perimeter.
launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.need: The park is much larger than it appears on a neighborhood map. Save a destination pin, allow time for hills and internal walking, and check attraction, restroom, water-feature, and event hours separately.

launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.address: Grand Central Parkway and Van Wyck Expressway, Queens, NY 11368
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.summary: Queens' 871-acre flagship park surrounds the Unisphere, World's Fair landmarks, museums, sports venues, playgrounds, Meadow Lake, and major recreation facilities.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.hours: Open daily 6 AM-1 AM; museums, recreation centers, sports venues, zoo, and playground facilities have separate schedules.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.parking: Parking is spread among destination-specific lots and can change during Mets games, US Open events, festivals, and construction. Do not assume the closest lot serves every attraction.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.arrival: The 7 train at Mets-Willets Point is the clearest arrival for the Unisphere, Queens Museum, and tennis center. Southern lake and playground destinations require a longer walk or a different street-side approach.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.restrooms: NYC Parks lists comfort stations at Carousel Loop, Playground for All Children, Ederle Terrace, Meadow Lake Boathouse, several playgrounds, and other park zones. Typical city restroom hours begin around 8 AM and extend later seasonally.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.cost: Park entry and outdoor landmarks are free. Museums, the zoo, tennis events, recreation facilities, rentals, and concessions may charge.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.accessibility: Many major promenades and attractions are accessible, but the park is enormous and highway or rail barriers make routes indirect. Use destination-specific accessible entrances.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.dogs: Dogs must be leashed except in designated dog-run or off-leash areas. Pets are not allowed in playgrounds, zoo exhibits, or ticketed venues unless they are service animals.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.family: The Playground for All Children, multiple themed playgrounds, zoo, science museum, Queens Museum, lake, and open lawns support full-day family visits.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.transit: Take the 7 train to Mets-Willets Point for the central World's Fair area. Q48 and other buses serve perimeter approaches; walking distances within the park remain substantial.
launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.need: Tide Gate Bridge construction currently blocks vehicular crossing on Meridian Road while pedestrians may still cross. Event traffic and venue security can significantly change arrival patterns.

launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.address: Gansevoort Street to West 34th Street, Manhattan, NY 10011
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.summary: The High Line is a 1.45-mile elevated linear park with gardens, public art, overlooks, seating, seasonal food, and connections through Chelsea and Hudson Yards.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.hours: Summer hours are generally daily 7 AM-11 PM; closing times change seasonally and weather or maintenance can close sections.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.parking: There is no park parking. Nearby garages are expensive and street parking is scarce; subway, bus, walking, or biking to a chosen entrance is more reliable.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.arrival: Choose an entrance based on the section you want. Elevators are listed at Gansevoort, 14th, 23rd, and 30th Streets, with ramp access at Hudson Yards; verify elevator status before an accessible visit.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.restrooms: Public restrooms are available near Gansevoort Street, West 16th Street, and West 30th Street. The long narrow route makes planning the next restroom important.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.cost: Entry is free. Food, shop purchases, and some partner experiences cost extra.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.accessibility: The park is wheelchair accessible through elevators and ramps, but individual elevators can be out of service. The route can be crowded and seating intervals vary.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.dogs: Dogs and other pets are prohibited, except service animals.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.family: Children often enjoy the train tracks, overlooks, art, and seating steps, but this is a linear promenade rather than a playground park. Hold hands near busy paths and exits.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.transit: The A/C/E and L serve 14th Street; 1/2/3 and 7 serve the northern area; buses run along Ninth, Tenth, and Eleventh Avenues.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.need: Bicycles, scooters, skating, smoking, picking plants, and climbing on railings or art are prohibited. Crowds are lighter near opening and on the northern sections.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.notice: Check the official access page the day of travel because elevator outages and temporary section closures can change the usable route.

launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.summary: This 85-acre East River park links six piers, lawns, playgrounds, sports, gardens, beaches, food, ferry landings, and classic bridge and skyline views.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.hours: Open daily 6 AM-1 AM. Playgrounds are sunrise-sunset and individual piers, restrooms, Water Lab, sports, and seasonal attractions keep shorter hours.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.parking: Parking is very limited. Transit, ferry, biking, and walking are recommended; limited metered spaces are near Pier 2 and paid garages are near Piers 1 and 6.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.arrival: Fulton Ferry Landing and DUMBO entrances serve the north; 360 Furman Street serves the south. NYC Ferry stops at Fulton Ferry Landing and Pier 6.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.restrooms: Restrooms are at Pier 1 Pavilion, Pier 2, Pier 5 Boathouse, Pier 6, Squibb Park, 99 Plymouth, and Empire Stores. March-October hours are generally 7 AM-11 PM and winter hours are shorter.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.cost: Park entry is free and most public programming is free. Food, carousel, rink, concessions, and some recreation cost extra.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.accessibility: Promenades and major piers are accessible. Access-A-Ride can use 1 Water Street for Pier 1 or 360 Furman Street for the south end.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.dogs: Dogs must be leashed and remain on permitted paths except in designated dog runs. Dogs are not allowed on lawns, playgrounds, sports surfaces, or beaches.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.family: Pier 6 playgrounds and Water Lab, Pier 2 sports, lawns, Jane's Carousel, Pebble Beach, and ferry views make this one of the city's strongest family park clusters.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.transit: A/C, 2/3, 4/5, F, and R trains plus several buses serve different edges. Ferry stops can eliminate long walks between the street grid and waterfront.
launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.need: Swimming and wading at Pier 4 Beach are prohibited because of strong currents, vessel traffic, cold water, and water quality. Waterfront weather changes quickly; check park alerts before events.

launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.summary: Hudson River Park spans four miles and 550 acres along Manhattan's west side, connecting piers, playgrounds, lawns, sports, beaches, food, science, and river access.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.hours: Open daily 6 AM-1 AM unless posted otherwise. Individual piers, rooftops, playgrounds, restrooms, concessions, and partner attractions have separate hours.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.parking: There is no single park lot and west-side parking is expensive. Transit, walking, biking, and choosing a cross street for the intended pier are usually best.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.arrival: Plan by pier number and cross street rather than using the general park address. The park extends from Tribeca to West 59th Street, so arriving at the wrong section can add miles.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are distributed at Pier 25, Pier 40, Pier 45, Pier 51, Gansevoort Peninsula, Little Island, Pier 57, Chelsea Waterside, Pier 84, Pier 97, and other facilities; hours vary by location and season.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.cost: Park entry, public lawns, many playgrounds, and many programs are free. Commercial attractions, food, rentals, and some activities charge.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.accessibility: Major park paths and public restrooms are accessible, but some piers and partner spaces have distinct routes, elevators, and schedules.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted on designated paths and dog runs are available, but dogs are excluded from lawns, playgrounds, beaches, and some piers or partner spaces.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.family: Pier 25, Pier 51, Chelsea Waterside, Gansevoort Peninsula, Pier 57, Little Island, sports fields, and river ecology programs provide varied family options.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.transit: Multiple subway lines and crosstown buses reach neighborhoods east of the park. Expect an additional walk west to the river after leaving transit.
launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.need: The adjacent Hudson River Greenway bikeway is not part of the park and moves quickly; cross it carefully at marked locations. Pier-specific rules and restroom hours should be checked before a long visit.

launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.address: State Street and Battery Place, New York, NY 10004
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.summary: The Battery is a 25-acre harbor park with perennial gardens, Battery Playscape, SeaGlass Carousel, Castle Clinton, lawns, monuments, and ferry connections.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.hours: The outdoor park is generally open daily 6 AM-1 AM. Battery Playscape, Castle Clinton, restrooms, SeaGlass Carousel, and ferry facilities keep shorter schedules.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.parking: There is no park parking. Lower Manhattan garages are costly and street parking is extremely limited; subway or ferry connections are the practical choice.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.arrival: Bowling Green serves the north edge, Whitehall serves the Staten Island Ferry side, and Battery Maritime Building is east of the park. Statue of Liberty ferries depart near Castle Clinton.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.restrooms: Public restrooms are outside the restaurant, at Castle Clinton, and near the Battery Bikeway on Battery Place, generally 9 AM-4:30 PM; ferry terminals have separate facilities.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.cost: Park entry, gardens, Playscape, and Castle Clinton entry are free. SeaGlass rides cost $6 and Statue Cruises tickets are separate.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.accessibility: Main promenades and Playscape routes are accessible. Ferry security, historic structures, and carousel boarding have their own procedures.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on designated paths but not in playgrounds or planted areas. Follow posted rules near ferry queues and monuments.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.family: Battery Playscape, SeaGlass Carousel, harbor views, lawns, gardens, and ferries make a strong family stop, but attraction hours do not match the full park day.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.transit: Use 1 at South Ferry, R/W at Whitehall, 4/5 at Bowling Green, or nearby J/Z. The Staten Island Ferry terminal and Governors Island ferry are close but separate.
launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.need: Statue of Liberty ferry tickets and security are not operated by the park; use the authorized operator and arrive early. Carousel hours are seasonal and weather-sensitive.

launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.address: Between 40th and 42nd Streets and Fifth and Sixth Avenues, New York, NY 10018
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.summary: Bryant Park is Midtown's compact public living room, combining a central lawn, movable chairs, gardens, carousel, games, reading room, food, events, and winter skating.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.hours: May-September: daily 7 AM-11 PM. October and January-April: 7 AM-10 PM. November-December hours extend to midnight Thursday-Sunday.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.parking: There is no park parking and Midtown driving is slow and expensive. Subway, bus, walking, or nearby commercial garages are the realistic options.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.arrival: Fifth Avenue places you beside the library; Sixth Avenue is closest to the lawn and many activities. The park occupies one city block, so internal navigation is simple.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.restrooms: Staffed public restrooms are on the 42nd Street and 40th Street sides, with changing facilities and accessible fixtures. Summer hours generally extend to 11 PM but maintenance can shorten them.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.cost: Park entry, chairs, lawn access, reading room, and many games and events are free. Carousel, food, rentals, and some seasonal services charge.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.accessibility: Level perimeter entrances and paved promenades make most areas accessible. The lawn can close after rain or for event setup.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted on paved areas but not on the central lawn. Owners must follow posted event and seasonal restrictions.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.family: Le Carrousel, games, children's reading programs, lawn time, food, performances, and winter skating work well for short family visits.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.transit: B/D/F/M and 7 trains stop at 42 St-Bryant Park/Fifth Avenue; many buses run on Fifth, Sixth, and 42nd Street.
launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.need: The lawn is not guaranteed to be open every day because rain, turf care, and large events require closures. Check the daily lawn message and event calendar.

launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.address: 10 South Street, Slip 7, New York, NY 10004
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.summary: Governors Island is a car-free harbor destination with hills, slides, hammocks, lawns, historic districts, art, food, cycling, and skyline views reached by ferry.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.hours: Open daily year-round. Current hours are 7 AM-10 PM Sunday-Thursday and 7 AM-11 PM Friday-Saturday; South Island Park closes at dusk.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.parking: Visitors cannot drive onto the island. Use transit to the ferry; paid garages are available in Lower Manhattan, but ferry schedules make transit the better option.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.arrival: Trust ferries depart from the Battery Maritime Building at 10 South Street. Seasonal weekend service also runs from Brooklyn Bridge Park Pier 6 and Red Hook; NYC Ferry is a separate operator.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are in Building 110 near Soissons Landing and in trailers at Yankee Pier, Liggett Terrace on weekends, and South Battery.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.cost: Island entry is free, but ferry fares may apply. Trust-operated ferries are free for select riders and during designated morning trips; rentals, food, and attractions charge separately.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.accessibility: Ferries and grounds are wheelchair accessible, though not every historic building is. A seasonal accessible tram runs approximately every 30 minutes between ferry landings.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.dogs: Pets are generally not permitted except service animals and dogs participating in specifically announced programs. Confirm current island rules before traveling.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.family: Slide Hill, Hammock Grove, Play Lawns, fountains at Liggett Terrace, cycling, picnics, and open space make the island a high-value family day trip.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.transit: Use 1, R/W, 4/5, J/Z, or buses to Lower Manhattan and walk to the Battery Maritime Building. Brooklyn ferry service is seasonal.
launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.need: A ferry is required, the South Island closes at dusk, and return lines can grow near closing. The kayak dock at Pier 101 is currently out of service for repairs.

launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.address: Riverside Drive from West 59th to West 181st Streets, New York, NY
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.summary: Riverside Park and Riverside Park South form a long Hudson River landscape with playgrounds, sports, lawns, gardens, monuments, cafés, trails, and Pier I.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.hours: Open daily 6 AM-1 AM. Playgrounds, cafés, courts, restrooms, and programmed areas have shorter or seasonal hours.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.parking: There is no single park lot. Street parking is limited and entrances are separated by steep grades, rail lines, and the highway; arrive near the intended cross street.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.arrival: Use West 72nd for Riverside Park South and Pier I, West 91st for Hippo Playground and the garden, West 96th for tennis and Dinosaur Playground, or destination-specific entrances farther north.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.restrooms: Restrooms are distributed at Pier I, Classic, Elephant, River Run, Hippo and Dinosaur playgrounds, clay tennis courts, Ellington, Grant's Tomb area, and several northern playgrounds.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.cost: Park entry, playgrounds, lawns, gardens, and most outdoor areas are free. Tennis permits, food, rentals, and some organized programs cost extra.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.accessibility: The park's multiple levels and steep slopes make route selection important. Riverside Park South is broadly accessible, while some historic upper-park paths use stairs or steep ramps.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.dogs: Dogs must be leashed except in designated runs or posted off-leash areas. Quiet lawns, playgrounds, sports areas, and gardens have additional restrictions.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.family: Numerous destination playgrounds, Pier I, lawns, sports, river views, cafés, and free seasonal programming support repeat family visits.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.transit: The 1/2/3 and multiple buses serve the Upper West Side, but most stops remain east of Riverside Drive. Match the station to the destination's cross street.
launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.need: Riverside Park is six miles long and split across elevations. Search by named playground, pier, or cross street instead of navigating to the park's center point.
